newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares swept through closing and intra-day highs on Monday, rising on a firmer dollar and an early Wall Street surge although dealers said volume was thin and many in the markets mistrusted the advance.

"This is all on an empty market and without the big volumes you can't really trust this rise," said one dealer, adding that domestic interest rates were close to bottoming out and the outlook for U.S. rates was uncertain.
The AEX share index closed 5.04 points higher at 576.96, pushing ahead from last Friday's record close and easily beating the previous all time high of 574.25 set on Thursday.

Chartists said earlier they were staying broadly neutral on the AEX until it went convincingly through resistance at 572.50. "A running start is needed to breach this resistance," said ING Barings in a research note, published this morning.

"However, underlying technicals of the AEX remain solid and sound. We expect another test of resistance at 572.50 any time soon. We will upgrade our technical rating for the AEX if the market closes above 572.50 on heavy volume," it said.
Others are more positive, citing the recent Dutch budget and the Fed's actions to stave off a U.S. interest rate rise as positive background factors for the market.
Dealers said trading throughout the session had been tranquil as market players carried out routine book squaring ahead of the end-quarter with little major corporate news on the immediate horizon.
This, they said, was squeezing prices higher than they might have otherwise gone. "If you can't pick up the stock and the price just moves away from you that's not so healthy," one said.

Publishers were the market's favourites on Monday, pushing up on talk of cyclical demand and a covered warrant put through the market. Wolters Kluwer climbed 7.80 guilders to 215.30 and VNU put on 1.70 to 33.50 guilders.

Royal Dutch closed 3.00 guilders up at 267.50 supported by Friday's late surge in oil prices and helped by the dollar strength. Unilever, another major dollar earner, slipped to be down 1.10 guilders to 270.10, hurt after brokerage Kleinwort Benson issued a sell note.

Polygram, the 75-percent owned movies and music unit of Philips, added 4.10 guilders to 95.80. Dealers said U.S. buyers had been picking up the stock which was moving up to keep pace with a recent climb in Philips. Philips itself was 10 cents higher at 61.80 guilders. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
